evidence_excerpts: Applying a remote CNOT has a computational complexity of O(n), with n being the number of QPUs. Given that we need at most n/4 swaps, the computational complexity of Algorithm 2 turns out to be O(n2). The overall computational complexity of distributing a circuit is, therefore, O(dn2).
text: The proposed compiler is computationally efficient because distributing a circuit has O(d n squared) complexity, with d the circuit depth and n the number of QPUs or logical qubits in the modeled worst case.
